episodes.177858: A cold front produced a squall that resulted in a few wind gusts to gale force.
episodes.177893: A very deeply mixed boundary layer developed on the afternoon of the 17th ahead of a surface trough in eastern New Mexico. Minimal convective inhibition and a weak approaching short wave allowed for a few high based storms to develop. Inverted-V sounding profiles allowed these storms to produce strong wind gusts at the surface. One storm produced a severe wind gust near Hart (Castro County).
episodes.178469: Brief funnel cloud observed near Pine Island in association with convection ahead of a cold front moving across the eastern Gulf of Mexico.
episodes.178844: A deeper than average snow pack from northern Minnesota and northern Wisconsin underwent a rapid melt through much of April from unseasonably warm temperatures and multiple rain events. This resulted in increased water levels and significant flooding for the entire length of the local Mississippi River, with most sites climbing to their third to fifth highest crests on record. In response to the widespread flooding, the Governor of Iowa issued a Proclamation of Disaster Emergency for counties along the Mississippi River. Initial flood warnings were issued in mid April with peak stages realized towards late April. The highest above flood stage was Guttenberg Dam at 6.91 ft over flood stage.
episodes.178849: A deeper than average snow pack from northern Minnesota into northern Wisconsin underwent a rapid melt through much of April from unseasonably warm temperatures combined with multiple rain events. This resulted in increased water levels and significant flooding for the entire length of the local Mississippi River, with most sites climbing to their third to fifth highest crests on record. A significant mid-April rain and snow event resulted in the Governor of Wisconsin issuing a State of Emergency declaration for flooding on April 16, 2023. Initial flood warnings were issued in mid April with peak stages realized in late April. The highest above flood stage was Lynxville Dam at 5.26 ft over flood stage.
episodes.178852: A deeper than average snow pack from northern Minnesota into northern Wisconsin underwent a rapid melt through much of April from unseasonably warm temperatures combined with multiple rain events. This resulted in increased water levels and significant flooding for the entire length of the local Mississippi River, with most sites climbing to their third to fifth highest crests on record. Initial flood warnings were issued in mid April with peak stages realized in late April. The highest above flood stage was Winona Dam at 5.81 ft over flood stage.
episodes.178867: Snowmelt resulted in flooding along the James River and its associated tributaries. The National Weather Service recorded an April record snow depth of 26 inches in Aberdeen on the 5th. This was followed by near normal temperatures through the latter half of the month of April. This relatively mild warmup resulted in snowmelt on top of frozen ground, and forced most of the melt into the waterways. River gauges near Columbia peaked just below major flood stage at 17.85 feet on April 30th and near Stratford just below moderate flood stage with 16.75 feet on April 30th. The gauge near Ashton peaked well above major flood stage at 19.91 feet on April 21st, which overtopped one of the bridges and impacted another near the gauge site. The gauge near Redfield peaked at 22.3 feet on April 22nd, just above moderate flood stage. Aside from the bridges and a few roads that were impacted, the main result of this high water was flooding of agricultural lands.
episodes.179012: Much of the Elm River drainage basin experienced a cold slow start to spring, leaving the ground frozen when temperatures finally started to consistently warm above freezing during the second week in April. Snow water equivalent at the start of April was in excess of 4 inches, with most of the melt entering waterways and the resultant flooding mainly affecting agricultural lands.||A Presidential Disaster Declaration was approved for Brown, Clark, Codington, Day, Faulk, Grant, Hand, Marshall, Potter and Roberts Counties, as well as for the Lake Traverse Indian Reservation, where an estimated $2,305,362 in total qualifying costs were incurred during spring flooding.
episodes.179032: Much of the Maple River drainage basin experienced a cold slow start to spring, leaving the ground frozen when temperatures finally started to consistently warm above freezing during the second week in April. Snow water equivalent at the start of April was in excess of 4 inches, with most of the melt entering waterways with the resulting flooding of the Maple. The gauge near Frederick crested at 12.36 feet, or 2.36 feet above flood stage. At this level, water reaches the bottom of the bridge 1 mile south of the gauge, while the bridges 1 mile north of the gauge and 2 miles north of the gauge site are overtopped. Additionally, a wide area of agricultural lands were inundated.||A Presidential Disaster Declaration was approved for Brown, Clark, Codington, Day, Faulk, Grant, Hand, Marshall, Potter and Roberts Counties, as well as for the Lake Traverse Indian Reservation, where an estimated $2,305,362 in total qualifying costs were incurred during spring flooding.
episodes.179044: A cold front extending from a strong upper level low moved across the area during the evening hours of the 16th. Ahead of the front, building instability on an unseasonably warm day resulted in a few severe thunderstorms over far western New York, including the Buffalo Metro. A severe wind gust of 59 mph was measured at the Buffalo Airport during the evening hours.
episodes.179046: A cold front extending from a strong upper level low moved across the area during the evening hours of the 16th. Ahead of the front, building instability on an unseasonably warm day resulted in a few severe thunderstorms over far western New York, including the Buffalo Metro. A severe wind gust of 59 mph was measured at the Buffalo Airport during the evening hours.
episodes.179105: On April 13th through April 17th, the South Pacific Convergence Zone (SPCZ) moved over the territory. Rainfall reported at the WSO Pago Pago office was 5.21 inches throughout this time. Embedded heavy rainfall within the SPCZ caused flash flooding across Tutuila Island. US Park Service rain gauge recorded 1.39 inches of rain between 1323SST and 1423SST on April 15th. WSO Pago Pago received 1.18 inches of rain between 1350SST and 1550SST.
episodes.179263: A shortwave trough and frontal boundary migrated across south Florida, which including daytime heating, brought multiple rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms to the east coast metro in South Florida April 16th and overnight into the 17th.
episodes.179264: As a shortwave moved across the Florida Peninsula, abundant low-level moisture and diurnal heating led to plenty of instability in the atmosphere on April 17th. Numerous showers and thunderstorms formed in the evening over the interior which moved offshore into the Atlantic overnight.
episodes.179265: A cold front moved across the Florida Peninsula and lingered in South Florida keeping a lot of moisture in the region on April 17th. With a shortwave trough aloft, it provided an extra source of lift for an afternoon and evening convection. Showers and thunderstorms brought heavy rain, hail, and gusty winds to the eastern metropolitan area.
episodes.179586: Rapid melting of much above normal snowpack caused widespread, and at times, extensive flooding over portions of west and central Upper Michigan from the 12th into the 25th.  Extensive impacts from the flooding caused Governor Whitmer to declare a state of emergency declaration for eight counties in west and central Upper Michigan on the 21st.
episodes.180044: Snowmelt flooding along the North Dakota Tributaries began in early to mid-April, with a few locations persisting into early May.
episodes.180055: Snowmelt flooding along the Minnesota Tributaries began in mid-April, with a few locations persisting into early May.
episodes.180131: Gale-force wind gusts occurred in the Lower Florida Keys coastal waters as showers and thunderstorms moved rapidly northeast from the western Straits of Florida.  A cold front was approaching from the northwest over the offshore southeast Gulf of Mexico.
episodes.180132: Several waterspouts were observed oceanside of Islamorada as showers and thunderstorms developed in advance of an approaching cold front.

Significant upstream runoff from the combination of rainfall and melting snow pushed the Mississippi River at McGregor into flood stage on April 16th. The crest of 22.91 ft on April 28th was 6.91 ft over flood stage. Much of McGregor's downtown riverfront area was closed due to being underwater. North of neighboring Marquette, Iowa, Highway 76 was closed due to flooding from Highway 18 to north of Effigy Mounds. In both towns, people were evacuated from their homes due to rising flood waters.
A few secondary roads were closed north of Newberry due to snowmelt runoff over the roads.

Significant upstream runoff from the combination of rainfall and melting snow pushed the Mississippi River at La Crosse into flood stage on April 17th. The crest of 15.89 ft on April 26 was 3.89 ft over flood stage. Multiple parks were closed due to flood waters, including Pettibone Park which was fully submerged and sustained significant road damage. French Island, which abuts La Crosse, had a voluntary evacuation order in place. People were forced to pump water from their basements around the clock and used canoes in the streets.

Significant upstream runoff from the combination of rainfall and melting snow pushed the Mississippi River at Genoa into flood stage on April 17th. The crest of 635.72 ft above sea level on April 27 was 4.72 ft over flood stage. Water flowed through Genoa Park and into Water Street. Lock & Dam 8 in Genoa was closed, as was Blackhawk Island a few miles downstream in De Soto. The increased flow also resulted in multiple train cars being carried downstream during a train derailment near De Soto on April 27th. Flooded roadside ditches made further recovery efforts into May more challenging.
